thought.text: The probe results are paradoxical: `terms_data_protection=` works but `terms_of_service=` doesn't, and validations pass with nil. Let me get ground truth from the console:

reasoning_content:
This is strange — `terms_data_protection` was set without any issue, yet I can't find any accessor definition. Wait — maybe it's because `User` responds to arbitrary setters via `method_missing`? No, ActiveRecord doesn't do that.

Let me think again: in the probe, `u.terms_data_protection = "1"` output OK. And `u.terms_of_service = "1"` raised NoMethodError. So terms_data_protection really does have a writer, and terms_of_service doesn't.

Where could that writer be coming from? Maybe there's a `terms_data_*` column in the schema that I missed because of case differences in the search? I grepped `t\.\(boolean\|string\|integer\) "terms` in db/schema.rb — exit 1, no match. And `grep "terms"` db/schema.rb returned nothing (the combined output of the earlier `grep -n "terms" db/schema.rb` and the psql output had no lines before ---live DB---). So the schema really doesn't have a terms column.

Hmm, wait — maybe the live database has columns that the schema.rb I'm looking at doesn't? No — the psql dump of users columns showed all 94 columns, and there were no terms columns.

Then where is the writer? Maybe it's `acts_as_votable` or some gem... no, that's not it. Let me check `method_missing`, or check if there's a `Terms` concern being included. Actually — wait. Maybe there's an `attr_writer` via `attr_accessor` on line 29 — I only looked at lines 29–32 (the form_registered_address group). Let me look at the entire attribute declaration area and search for "terms" across all custom model files and concerns.

No, hold on. Let me reconsider: does AR respond to `u.terms_data_protection = "1"` by raising UnknownAttributeError (NoMethodError) at assignment time? In Rails 6.1, `ActiveModel::AttributeAssignment#_assign_attribute` → if the attribute doesn't exist → raises `ActiveModel::UnknownAttributeError` (a subclass of NameError)... actually:

```ruby
def _assign_attribute(attr, value, &block)
  # ...
  if method_attributes.include?(attr) || ...
```

Hmm, in `AttributeAssignment`:
```ruby
if attr = self.class._default_attributes.key?(attr_name.to_s) ...
```

Actually the logic is: `if respond_to?(attr_name)` etc. For an unknown attribute at assignment, it raises `ActiveModel::UnknownAttributeError`. No wait:

```ruby
def _assign_attribute(attr, value, &block)
  if attr = self.class.attribute_types[attr] ...
```

Let me recall exactly (Rails 6.1):

```ruby
def assign_attributes(new_attributes)
  new_attributes.each do |key, value|
    key = key.to_s
    if key.end_with?("=�")
      ...
    else
      _assign_attribute(key, value, &block)
    end
  end
end

def _assign_attribute(attr, value, &block)
  # ...
  unless self.class._default_attributes.key?(attr) || method_attributes.include?(attr.to_sym)
    ...raise
```

Hmm, what I actually remember is:

```ruby
private
  def _assign_attribute(key, value, &block)
    if key = self.class._default_attributes[key]
      ...
    elsif respond_to?("#{key}=") || respond_to?(key, true)
      ...
    else
      raise UnknownAttributeError.new(self, key)
    end
  end
```

So `assign_attributes(terms_of_service: "1")` raises UnknownAttributeError — which is exactly the error the seed threw: `ActiveModel::UnknownAttributeError: unknown attribute 'terms_of_service' for User.` And my direct setter call `u.terms_of_service = "1"` → NoMethodError. Consistent: no such writer exists.

But `u.terms_data_protection = "1"` didn't raise an exception → a writer exists → the attribute exists → it must be in `_default_attributes` or a method. But `User.column_names` doesn't include it...

Ah, wait. I think I've got it! Globalize! The model might be using `translates :terms_data_storage` or a similar Globalize attribute. Globalize adds attributes. No, more likely: `acts_as_paranoid`? No, that's not it.

Hmm, what about `audited`? No, that's not it either.

Let me just check directly in the console: `User.attribute_names.include?("terms_data_protection")`, `User.attribute_types.keys`, and `User.new.respond_to?(:terms_data_protection=)`. That will settle it.

Also `User.new.valid?` returned TRUE without terms being set — meaning the acceptance validation passed without the attributes being set! This can happen if the validation callback checks something like `validates ... unless: :guest?` — no, terms_data_protection is `on: :create` unconditionally. `valid?` triggers the :create context validations. If the attribute were nil and there were no `unless`, it should fail... unless the validation didn't actually get registered! If `validates :terms_data_protection` referenced a non-existent attribute... Rails' `validates` with a symbol → uses `respond_to?`... no, the validator calls `record.send(:terms_data_protection)` during validate → NoMethodError at validation time, not skipped.

Hmm, unless the model doesn't include those validations — wait, is the custom file actually being applied? With `config.autoload_paths << Rails.root.join("app/models/custom")` and the classic autoloader — does the file `app/models/custom/user.rb` define `class User < ApplicationRecord`?? It can't redeclare as a subclass... let me look at the first few lines of custom/user.rb — I've only seen the middle of the file. I need to verify that it opens `class User` (reopening) and not some other class.

Actually, in probe #1 I set all three terms values and `u.valid?` → true. If those were real validations on real attributes, setting "1" would pass acceptance anyway. OK.

But the key question is: does `User.new(terms_of_service: "1")` work after my fix? My probe showed NoMethodError → the seed as written fails on users (and probably on other terms_of_service seeds too).

Wait, wait. Let me double-check: maybe the custom model adds the attribute with `attribute :terms_data_protection, ...`? I grepped `^\s*attribute\b` in custom/user.rb and user.rb — only line 3 of user.rb matched (`attribute :registering_from_web`). So it's not that.

OK, another possibility: the `Verification` concern (included by User) or a `concerns` file has `attr_writer :terms_data_protection` or `store` (AR store on a JSON/serialized column!). `store :something, accessors: [...]` creates virtual accessors! Let me search the whole app for "store :" on user-related models.

Let me run a comprehensive console probe:
- User.attribute_names.grep(/terms/)
- User.new.respond_to?(:terms_data_protection=)
- User.new.respond_to?(:terms_of_service=)
- User.validators

That will give me the ground truth.

puts "attribute_names terms: #{User.attribute_names.grep(/terms/).inspect}"
puts "respond_to terms_data_protection=: #{u.respond_to?(:terms_data_protection=)}"

puts "custom file def: #{User.instance_method(:terms_data_protection).source_location rescue "n/a"}"
' 2>&1 | tail -8
